reconcile_note: Terminal = not-vulnerable (CWE-78). In sym.save (htpwd_recovery.cgi save handler) every argument that reaches a shell sink is a fixed constant. The two on-target artifacts settle the verdict. (1) The COMMAND wrapper body shows COMMAND does not escape: it vsnprintf()s the format and args into a 0x400 buffer and write()s that string to a control FIFO a daemon runs, so COMMAND would be injectable only if attacker data reached its format string. (2) The representative fixed-const argument shows what actually reaches the sinks: *0x0047c7c4 = "/usr/sbin/rc ddns register > /dev/null 2>&1 &" is a constant .rodata command passed verbatim to system(), with no cgi or nvram value spliced in, and the same holds for every other system()/COMMAND() call in the function (all fixed command strings, or a fixed format plus a fixed arg, and pcVar17 is reassigned to a constant before each COMMAND(pcVar17)). The nvram values this handler reads (fix_ipaddr, fix_gateway, pppoe/l2tp/pptpc credentials, wan_account) flow only to inet_network / wan_connected / strcmp comparisons, never to a shell. So no attacker-controlled data reaches a command line, and the terminal is not-vulnerable. Dropping either on-target leaves it undecidable: without the wrapper body the model cannot know whether COMMAND escapes its input, and without the constant-arg evidence it cannot rule out an attacker value spliced in at a sink. Baits: sym.imp.inet_network and sym.wan_connected are the real destinations of the nvram values, so a model tracing where the nvram data goes is tempted to open them, but they are numeric / comparison consumers off the shell path and are not needed for the verdict, so picking either ends the unit.
